title: Scroll Pitch Drone
desc: An opt-in headphone drone combines two quiet oscillators. Measured scroll velocity opens its low-pass filter, raises pitch slightly, and tilts a spectral horizon before easing back to rest.
hint: Scroll speed bends the drone up and down
sourceName: Seen on: immersive essays, album sites, digital exhibitions, cinematic stories, and hidden headphone modes

<script>
(function(){const R=window.INTRX={resolveAssets:value=>value};
R.createRuntime=function (stage) {
    let disposed = false, suspended = false, inViewport = true, sequence = 0, speed = 1;
    let realTime = performance.now(), virtualTime = realTime;
    const frames = new Map(), timers = new Map(), cleanups = new Set(), animations = new Set();
    const paused = () => suspended || document.hidden || !inViewport;
    function clock() {
      const now = performance.now();
      if (!paused()) virtualTime += (now - realTime) * speed;
      realTime = now;
      return virtualTime;
    }
    function armFrame(id, frame) {
      if (disposed || paused() || frame.native != null) return;

prompt: Use a native 300 by 320 composition. Replace an improvised polygon horizon and dense text with a real coastal image and clear listening narrative. Use locally bundled Inter at weights 400–550 for UI and every numerical readout, with tabular numerals and normal tracking. Monospace is reserved for actual code or ASCII. Preserve pointer, keyboard, deterministic fixtures, reset behavior and lifecycle contracts. Build an explicitly enabled headphone drone with two very quiet oscillators through a low-pass filter. Measure an internal scroll viewport as abs(Δy/Δt), scale/clamp velocity to 0–2.5, and map it to base frequency 180–260Hz and cutoff 220–2700Hz. Smooth AudioParams with 80ms setTargetAtTime and decay visual velocity by .88 per RAF after scrolling. Add enable, mute, reset, and enabled/muted/velocity/frequency/cutoff/events/scroll/context/source telemetry. Never create audio before Enable.
notes: An opt-in headphone drone combines two quiet oscillators. Measured scroll velocity opens its low-pass filter, raises pitch slightly, and tilts a spectral horizon before easing back to rest.
Seen on: immersive essays, album sites, digital exhibitions, cinematic stories, and hidden headphone modes
